paper.title_en: Heat cleaning kinetics and thermal degradation of MOCVD-grown GaAs photocathodes
paper.abstract_en: We evaluated metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD)-grown GaAs/GaAsP strained-superlattice photocathodes with integrated distributed Bragg reflectors in a low-voltage Mott polarimeter at Jefferson Lab. Without a protective arsenic cap, surface contamination can develop during transport and installation. Heat cleaning removes this contamination by thermally desorbing material bound to the surface, but excessive heating can also damage the photocathode. We modeled quantum efficiency (QE) in terms of surface contaminant coverage to describe its increase with heating time. QE rose more rapidly and reached a plateau nearly twice as high at $550^\circ\text{C}$ as at $450^\circ\text{C}$, while polarization remained near 83%. Further heating reduced QE and polarization. Reflectance measurements showed a shift of the optical resonance to shorter wavelengths, consistent with surface material loss. We also tested the cleaning method in a high-voltage photogun, where QE showed the same initial increase and subsequent decline. The cleaning procedure must therefore balance contaminant removal against loss of photocathode material.
